title: ASML will be unable to meet AI-driven customer demand in 2027, 2028
source_used: RTE.ie and CTech, both carrying the same statement of ASML that Reuters reported (Reuters page returned HTTP 401)
key_facts: ASML said on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026 that AI-driven demand for its chipmaking equipment is so strong it will not be able to fully meet customer demand in 2027 or 2028.
ASML is looking at ways to expand capacity further; in July it said it would raise capacity by 30% in 2027 and by another 30% in 2028.
Fourth-quarter 2026 sales forecast: EUR 14.2 billion to 15.2 billion (about USD 15.9 to 17.0 billion), with a gross margin of around 57%.
Analysts polled by LSEG had expected fourth-quarter sales of EUR 14.19 billion, so the low end of the range is only just above expectations.
Chief executive Christophe Fouquet: customer talks are shifting beyond 2027, with a lot of order intake for 2028 and interest in orders for 2029 and sometimes 2030.
CTech adds that ASML now expects 2026 net sales of EUR 44 billion to 45 billion, raising the bottom of its range from EUR 43 billion.
quote_evidence: ASML said today that AI-driven demand for its chip-printing tools is so strong that it will not be able to fully meet customer demand in 2027 or 2028 and it is looking at ways to further expand capacity.
Analysts polled by LSEG had expected sales of €14.19 billion.
In July the company said it would increase capacity in 2027 by 30% and again by 30% in 2028.
why_it_matters_hint: ASML is the world's largest maker of chip-manufacturing equipment, so a capacity warning sets the pace of AI chip supply.
notes: Reuters page blocked (401). The same ASML statement, with the same figures and quotes, was read on RTE.ie and CTech and is also headlined by Anadolu, TradingKey and others. The Reuters byline is not shown on the RTE page, so the entry credits Reuters as the pool item does and says the statement is ASML's.
